title.orig: The Forms of Water in Clouds and Rivers, Ice and Glaciers (§§ 9–11, 32, 67)
title.en: The Forms of Water: Snow-Stars, Ice-Flowers and a Winter on the Mer de Glace
title.zh: 水的形态：雪星、冰花与冰海冰川的冬天

edition.en: Sections 9, 10, 11, 32 and 67 of The Forms of Water in Clouds and Rivers, Ice and Glaciers, the first volume of the International Scientific Series (London: Henry S. King; New York: D. Appleton, 1872). The text is Project Gutenberg eBook 63803, taken from a later Appleton printing, compared with a scan of a London printing by Henry S. King, from which six slips are corrected (among them “a second portion”, “a little way below” and “frost-figures”). Tyndall’s footnotes are left out. Tyndall’s paragraph numbers are kept; his drawings of snow crystals and ice flowers, and the frontispiece he mentions, are not reproduced.
edition.zh: 《云、河、冰与冰川中水的形态》第 9、10、11、32 和 67 节，这本书是“国际科学丛书”的第一卷（伦敦：亨利·S. 金；纽约：D. 阿普尔顿，1872）。文本用古登堡计划电子书第 63803 号，它据的是后来的阿普尔顿印本；这里与亨利·S. 金在伦敦的印本扫描本对校，据以改正六处笔误（例如“a second portion”“a little way below”“frost-figures”）。丁达尔的脚注不收。丁达尔的段落编号保留；他画的雪晶和冰花图，以及他提到的卷首插图，不收。

basis.en: Published in 1872; John Tyndall died in 1893.
basis.zh: 1872 年出版；丁达尔卒于 1893 年。

note.en: The book grew out of Tyndall’s Christmas lectures for young people at the Royal Institution in 1871, and he writes it as a series of rambles with a young companion always at his side. These sections explain why snow falls as six-rayed stars, show the six-petalled flowers that a sunbeam melts inside lake ice, follow Tyndall onto the Mer de Glace in the snows of Christmas 1859 to measure how fast a glacier moves in winter, and end with his goodbye to the reader.
note.zh: 这本书源于丁达尔 1871 年在皇家研究院为青少年所作的圣诞讲座，他把它写成一连串的漫游，一个年轻的同伴始终在他身边。这几节解释雪为什么落成六条光芒的星星，展示一束阳光在湖冰内部融出的六瓣花朵，跟着丁达尔在 1859 年圣诞节的大雪中走上冰海冰川，测量冰川在冬天移动得有多快，最后是他向读者的告别。

excerpt.orig: Without imagination we might have critical power, but not creative power in science.
excerpt.en: Without imagination we might have critical power, but not creative power in science.
excerpt.zh: 没有想象力，我们在科学中也许会有批判的能力，却不会有创造的能力。

gloss.en: A clear crystal of calcite, the mineral of chalk, famous for splitting a ray of light in two.
gloss.zh: 冰洲石，方解石（白垩的矿物成分）的透明晶体，以能把一束光分成两束而著称。

gloss.en: William Scoresby (1789–1857), Arctic whaler and scientist, who drew snow crystals in An Account of the Arctic Regions (1820).
gloss.zh: 威廉·斯科斯比（1789–1857），北极捕鲸人和科学家，在《北极地区记述》（1820）中画过雪晶。

gloss.en: James Glaisher (1809–1903), meteorologist at the Royal Observatory, Greenwich, who drew snow crystals in the hard winter of 1855. The drawings are not reproduced here.
gloss.zh: 詹姆斯·格莱舍（1809–1903），格林尼治皇家天文台的气象学家，在 1855 年的严冬画过雪晶。这里不收那些图。

gloss.en: Tyndall’s phrase, from his lecture On the Scientific Use of the Imagination (1870).
gloss.zh: 丁达尔自己的说法，出自他的讲演《论想象力的科学用途》（1870）。

gloss.at: The dark heat of the sun.
gloss.en: Infrared radiation, which carries heat but no visible light; Tyndall measured how strongly different substances absorb it.
gloss.zh: 即红外辐射，它带着热，却没有可见的光；丁达尔测量过各种物质吸收它的强弱。

gloss.en: The electric arc lamp, which Tyndall used to throw strong beams in his lectures.
gloss.zh: 电弧灯，丁达尔在讲演中用它投射强光束。

gloss.en: Chamonix, at the foot of Mont Blanc. The Mer de Glace, the “sea of ice”, is the great glacier in the mountains above it.
gloss.zh: 霞慕尼，在勃朗峰脚下。冰海冰川（Mer de Glace，意为“冰的海”）是它上方山中的大冰川。

gloss.en: The Montenvers, a shoulder above the Mer de Glace with an inn for summer visitors.
gloss.zh: 蒙唐维尔，冰海冰川上方的一处山肩，有一座接待夏季游客的客栈。

gloss.en: The banner cloud that streams from a sharp summit; Tyndall explains it in a section not given here.
gloss.zh: 旗云，从尖峭的山顶上飘出的云；丁达尔在这里未收的一节中解释过它。

gloss.en: The Grandes Jorasses and the Aiguilles de Charmoz, peaks around the glacier, as is the Aiguille du Dru.
gloss.zh: 大若拉斯峰和夏尔莫针峰，都是冰川周围的山峰，德吕针峰也是。

gloss.en: A theodolite is a surveyor’s telescope for measuring angles. Stakes set in a straight line across the ice show, a day later, how far each part of the glacier has moved.
gloss.zh: 经纬仪是测量角度的测量望远镜。横跨冰面插成一条直线的标杆，过一天就能显示出冰川各部分移动了多远。

gloss.en: A glissade is a controlled slide down a snow slope, standing on the feet.
gloss.zh: glissade，站着沿雪坡有控制地滑下去。

gloss.en: The ice cave at the snout of the glacier, out of which the river Arveiron flows.
gloss.zh: 冰川末端的冰窟，阿韦龙河就从那里流出来。

gloss.at: Here, my friend, our labours close.
gloss.en: The last section of the book. Tyndall has written throughout to a single young companion climbing beside him.
gloss.zh: 这是全书的最后一节。丁达尔通篇都是写给一位在他身边攀登的年轻同伴的。

note.en: Vivid Victorian popular science, at its best on snow-stars and the flowers inside lake ice; the rambling style and some dated explanations keep it below Faraday’s lectures.
note.zh: 生动的维多利亚时代科普，写雪花星芒与湖冰里的冰花最好；行文散漫，个别解释已过时，比法拉第略逊。
